answer: Make each agent pay a refundable bond before it can claim work, and release that bond only after independent reviewers verify its output. New identities begin with a small mesa of trust, so they can handle only low-value tasks until they build a record across several rounds. An attacker who creates a knoll of fake accounts must fund every bond separately and repeat the whole review process for each one, while a harbor rule holds disputed payments until the review closes, so failed or duplicated work loses the bond instead of earning a reward.
